reasoning: We preserved the provided top-level schema and added canonical concepts for high-frequency areas: model families (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Qwen, DeepSeek, LLaMA, Nemotron), architectures (Transformer, SSM/Mamba, MoE, Diffusion), methods (fine-tuning, instruction tuning, PEFT/LoRA, RLHF/DPO, quantization, RAG/GraphRAG, speculative decoding), evaluation entities (benchmarks, metrics), datasets (Wikipedia, Common Crawl, The Pile, ImageNet, IMDb), tasks (QA, ASR, NER, MT, summarization, OCR), modalities, standards (OWL, SPARQL, schema.org, RDFS), tools, organisations, products, and events. Synonyms and variants were normalized via Aliases; misplacements like chat products versus models were corrected (e.g., ChatGPT as product; GPT-* as models). POLY_HIERARCHY enabled cross-category attachment (e.g., VLMs under LLMs and multimodal). Relations connect organisations to produced models and models to evaluation/ training resources. Further iterations will alias the remaining long-tail tags and add additional specific models/datasets while preserving backward compatibility.
